Reviewable status: all files reviewed, 4 unresolved discussions (waiting on jolierabideau and tjcouch-sil). lib/platform-bible-react/.storybook/theme-apply.ts line 32 at r5 (raw file): Looks like we still have a naming scheme that doesn't reflect the two-axis way we're handling themes. Composite ID CSS classes on  Defined in shadcn-light ['theme-shadcn-neutral'] index.css:172 shadcn-dark ['dark', 'theme-shadcn-neutral'] index.css:205 platform-light [] (:root defaults) index.css:36 platform-dark ['dark'] index.css:70 paratext-light ['paratext-light'] index.css:102 paratext-dark ['paratext-dark'] In the latest commit (6512c8a6), the CSS selectors in index.css are: Selector Purpose Line :root, .light Platform light (default) 36-37 .dark Platform dark 70 .paratext-light Paratext light 102 .paratext-dark Paratext dark 136 .theme-shadcn-neutral Shadcn Neutral light (Storybook-only) 172 .dark.theme-shadcn-neutral Shadcn Neutral dark (Storybook-only) 205 Ask Devin: What is the naming scheme for the different themes and dark mode/light mode look like? How do they compare with best practice, and which files are they in? Devin sees what I'm getting at: 1. Inconsistent CSS class naming convention — The class names don't follow a single pattern: - Platform: `.light` / `.dark` (bare adjective) - Paratext: `.paratext-light` / `.paratext-dark` (family-prefixed) - Shadcn: `.theme-shadcn-neutral` + `.dark` (prefix `theme-` \+ compound) Best practice would be a uniform scheme, e.g. all `theme-{family}` with `.dark` as a modifier, or all `{family}-{scheme}`. The current mix of conventions means you need to memorize which pattern each family uses. This is partly inherited from the pre-existing `.dark` / `.paratext-*` classes that are shared with production (themes.data.json), so the inconsistency isn't entirely avoidable without a larger refactor. and more issues lib/platform-bible-react/src/stories/guidelines/theming-doc.tsx line 170 at r5 (raw file): Previously, jolierabideau wrote… These are valuable changes, I would prefer to do them in a separate PR if that's okay. This one is really big and I would like to get it merged! I'm not looking at the code because the file's deleted, but that makes sense about the "bad example" styling. As for the TSX part, I was under the impression that we could include what are essentially TSX blocks inside the MDX files, but maybe there's part of that or your situation that I don't understand? Update: but the bad example is missing a display of the code when I think the intention is to show the bad code lib/platform-bible-react/.storybook/theme-apply.ts line 68 at r8 (raw file): return DEFAULT_STORYBOOK_THEME_STATE; } } In contrast for the names above, these look great! Code quote: export function themeStateFromLegacyThemeId(themeId: StorybookThemeId): StorybookThemeState { switch (themeId) { case 'shadcn-light': return { family: 'shadcn-neutral', colorScheme: 'light' }; case 'shadcn-dark': return { family: 'shadcn-neutral', colorScheme: 'dark' }; case 'platform-light': return { family: 'platform', colorScheme: 'light' }; case 'platform-dark': return { family: 'platform', colorScheme: 'dark' }; case 'paratext-light': return { family: 'paratext', colorScheme: 'light' }; case 'paratext-dark': return { family: 'paratext', colorScheme: 'dark' }; default: return DEFAULT_STORYBOOK_THEME_STATE; } } lib/platform-bible-react/src/stories/guidelines/theming.mdx line 63 at r8 (raw file): **Paratext** is a separate palette (Caffeine-inspired in tweakcn), not vanilla Shadcn; it is not "mostly Slate." This section is where some of the naming confusion in the theme files starts to show up in the documentation. We should be seeing a 3x2 two-axis presentation of theme families and light/dark schemes here, but instead we're seeing four paragraphs, two of which are about families and two of which are about light/dark mode. If you need help terminology-wise, it can be a challenge to come up with names that convey each of these axes. I think I've seen Apple do it well, and this is what they call them. Appearance = light/dark/auto Theme > Color = multicolor, blue, green, red… We need names that have consistent meaning in our codebase and don't overlap or overload other names. So maybe we can treat theme as the overall concept and appearance as the light/dark system and color family as the other axis. Appearance includes: Display mode = light/dark/system, and Color theme* = Paratext (Caffeine) / Platform.Bible / Shadcn/neutral * (I'm also open to "color family" in case that's less confusing in the codebase) Would that work for you? I know this is a lot to be adding in at this point in the review process, but I want to be open about where my head's at before something different gets entrenched to minimize confusion. I'll also send a message to Sebastian about this. Code quote: ## Platform vs Shadcn Neutral vs Paratext CSS variables live in [index.css](https://github.com/paranext/paranext-core/blob/main/lib/platform-bible-react/src/index.css): Platform light is `:root` / `.light`; Platform dark is `.dark`; stock Shadcn Neutral is `.theme-shadcn-neutral` (and `.dark.theme-shadcn-neutral`); Paratext is `.paratext-light` / `.paratext-dark`. The running app loads Platform and Paratext HSLs from [themes.data.json](https://github.com/paranext/paranext-core/blob/main/src/shared/data/themes.data.json) (default Platform family key and `paratext`); Shadcn Neutral is Storybook-only. **Platform** default (`:root` / `.dark`) is **Slate-based** (blue-gray neutrals) but **not identical** to the stock Shadcn Neutral preset under `.theme-shadcn-neutral` in `storybook-themes.css`. Use the toolbar's **Shadcn Neutral** options when you need the closest match to [shadcn/ui docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming#neutral) for development, UX review, or debugging. Pick **Shadcn Neutral** under Theme and set Color scheme to light or dark (or system). **Light:** Platform differs from stock Neutral on **popover** (tinted vs pure white), **secondary / muted / accent** neutrals (Platform `210 50% 95%` vs Neutral `0 0% 96.1%`), and the full **sidebar-\*** token block (Platform stays Slate-aligned; Neutral follows the docs scaffold). **Dark:** Platform uses solid **border** / **input** grays; stock Neutral uses semi-transparent white on dark. Sidebar styling also differs (including Neutral's violet **sidebar-primary** in the docs preset). **Paratext** is a separate palette (Caffeine-inspired in tweakcn), not vanilla Shadcn; it is not "mostly Slate." lib/platform-bible-react/src/stories/guidelines/theming.mdx line 90 at r8 (raw file): Bad example

# Paratext / Platform.Bible branding in Storybook

This guide explains how the **Storybook manager** (outer chrome: sidebar, toolbar, panels) and the **preview iframe** (Canvas and Docs) can be aligned with Paratext or internal branding. Preview appearance combines **Color scheme** (light / dark / system) and **Theme** (Shadcn Neutral, Platform, Paratext), applied via [manager.tsx](./manager.tsx) (toolbars + direct iframe DOM update), [theme-apply.ts](./theme-apply.ts), and [theme-decorator.ts](./theme-decorator.ts) — not `globals.theme`, so Docs scroll is preserved when switching themes. Customizing the manager shell (logos, `brandTitle`, light/dark chrome) is **optional** and does not affect story output.

In flux. See discussion in https://ptb.discord.com/channels/892072317436448768/1492222711303241999/1492223016258633998
